Ahmadi's lawyer told Etemad that the singer and four members of her production team presented themselves to provincial authorities in the holy city of Qom, as required after their sentences were upheld in September by a local criminal court.

item.title: [CBS News World] Spacecraft enters Mercury's orbit after 8-year journey despite glitch
item.description:
A spacecraft has entered Mercury's orbit after an eight-year journey, overcoming a technical glitch to continue its mission to conduct scientific observations around the planet.
BepiColombo was launched as a joint mission between the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency in October 2018. Since then, it has navigated its way toward Mercury.
On Nov. 21, the spacecraft attached itself to Mercury's orbit. The maneuver started with a scheduled, brief loss of contact with the mission control team at the European Space Operations Center in Darmstadt, Germany, the ESA said in a news release.
As BepiColombo passed over the planet, it fired four axial thrusters that slowed it enough to lock into Mercury's orbit. During this stage of the mission, the spacecraft came within 400 miles of Mercury's surface. The burn was supposed to last for about 37 minutes.
BepiColombo fires its thrusters.
ESA
But when the ESA team reestablished contact with BepiColombo, they found the maneuver had been interrupted, causing the spacecraft to enter safe mode, where nonessential activities are stopped. Analysis of trajectory data showed the spacecraft had only completed about 77% of the maneuver.
"Upon finding Bepi in safe mode, it was like flipping a switch. Everybody was focused in understanding what had happened," ESA BepiColombo flight operations director Ignacio Tanco said in a statement.
The glitch has been traced to a software issue involving attitude guidance and thruster control, the ESA said. The investigation into the error is continuing.
Despite the error and the incomplete maneuver, ESA scientists were eventually able to confirm that BepiColombo had locked onto Mercury's orbit. It took six hours from the time...

How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEOByMichael RaceBusiness reporterPublished58 minutes ago
Shares in Nvidia dipped on Tuesday as US politicans questioned President Donald Trump's role in the return of Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Huang was handed back his job at the AI microchip maker on Monday less than two weeks after he was forced to resign following the revelations of extra marital affairs, one of which was with a suspected Chinese spy.
Trump has said he played a big role in the 63-year-old's reinstatment, which has led to questions and backlash from US lawmakers.
While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the annoucement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.
The company's share price was down almost 8% on Tuesday, but remained well above the level it closed at on Friday, before Huang's shock return was revealed.
However, Nvidia was not the only semiconductor chip company to experience share price declines on Tuesday, with rival AMD down more than 10%.
Broadcom and Marvell Technology shares were also lower, suggesting that investors were continuing to weigh up concerns over potential regulation by newly-elected Democrats, as well as the central question as to whether the huge amounts being invested in AI will pay off.
Nvidia's share price for example, is down almost 30% over the past six months and had been on the decline before the scandal involving its co-founder emerged earlier this month.
The company's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn on its original position. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

item.title: [ABC News World] Russia backs tax rises as 2027 budget sees military spending soar
item.description:
Russia backs tax rises as 2027 budget sees military spending soar
Russia’s lower house of parliament has approved a 2027-2029 state budget and passed tax increases to fund the war in UkraineByKATIE MARIE DAVIES Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 11:12 AM
Russia’s lower house of parliament approved a 2027-2029 state budget Tuesday and separately passed a series of tax increases to fund Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
The budget allocates approximately 17.15 trillion rubles ($208.9 billion) for national defense in 2027, up from the 12.93 trillion rubles ($157.5 billion) in 2026. The amount is also a marked increase from the 13.6 trillion rubles ($165.7 billion) forecast for expenditure in 2027 in last year’s budget.
The government seeks to help cover rising military costs with additional taxes on mining companies and income from citizens’ investments.
Deputies approved the bill with 396 votes in favor and 37 abstentions. It now goes to the Federation Council, Russia’s upper house of parliament, for approval.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has increasingly sought to squeeze tax revenue out of businesses and consumers to support his nearly five-year war in Ukraine, even as the country’s economy increasingly skews toward military spending at the expense of civilian needs.
Russia’s budget deficit has swelled beyond forecast this year because of heavy military spending and sluggish economic growth. The economy has also been strained by sanctions, high interest rates for nonmilitary companies, labor shortages and Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries and export terminals.
Dmitry Kobylkin, head of the parliamentary faction for the ruling United Russia party, hailed the bill as a “victory budget,” writing in a statement that it included spending on national defense and care for veterans and their families, as well as state social support.

item.title: [ABC News World] South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to travel to Russia to fight against Ukraine
item.description:
South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to travel to Russia to fight against Ukraine
A Zimbabwean man has been convicted in South Africa of trying to travel to Russia to fight in its war against UkraineByMOGOMOTSI MAGOME Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 10:50 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
JOHANNESBURG -- A Zimbabwean man was convicted and sentenced on Tuesday for trying to travel to Russia to fight in its war against Ukraine after being arrested in South Africa with eight others earlier this month.
Tafadzwa Sithole was sentenced to five years in prison, suspended for five years, and he is set to be deported back to Zimbabwe.
He told a South African court that he had agreed to fight for Russia in the war in exchange for “remuneration” after successfully applying online in Zimbabwe.
Sithole said a person he identified as “Albina” contacted him after he submitted the application, arranged accommodation in South Africa and provided a flight ticket to Russia.
His admissions were detailed in a plea agreement with South African prosecutors. He pleaded guilty to violating the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which prohibits mercenary activity and regulates military assistance to parties in foreign conflicts, including recruitment and training.
The law also applies to foreign nationals.
Sithole, who described himself as an unemployed third-year student at a university in Zimbabwe, appeared in court with four other accused who are also negotiating plea agreements with prosecutors.
He said he entered South Africa legally on Nov. 4 and stayed in accommodation in Kempton Park, east of Johannesburg, in preparation for his travel to Russia.
He was arrested at O.R. Tambo International Airport on Nov. 8 while attempting to board a flight to Russia.
“He agreed and offered to serve as a member of the armed forces of the Russian Federation in return for remuneration. He knew that the Russian Federation was engaged in an ongoing armed conflict with Ukr...

Gisèle Pelicot says she is shocked that a Paris publisher used nude images taken by her rapist ex-husband to promote a book about her caseByJOHN LEICESTER Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 11:02 AM
PARIS -- Gisèle Pelicot says she is deeply shocked that a Paris publishing house used nude images taken of her by her rapist ex-husband as promotional materials for a book that examines her watershed fight for justice.
The 73-year-old Pelicot became an icon of courage and feminist causes during the drugging-and-rape trial in 2024 that convicted all 51 of the accused men, including her ex-husband, Dominique Pelicot.
In a statement to BFMTV, Gisèle Pelicot denounced the book, “Emprises,” and the publisher’s use of intimate photos in promoting it. The broadcaster published extracts of the statement on Monday.
“I am deeply shocked that images of the most private aspects of my life could be exhibited and exploited for commercial gain," the statement said, according to BFMTV. “I refuse to let my private life be used as a selling point."
The nude images of Pelicot were apparently taken by Dominique Pelicot and were part of the court case that saw him sentenced to 20 years in prison, said Christophe Bigot, a lawyer for Gisèle Pelicot, speaking Tuesday to The Associated Press.
Bigot said he has seen the images and that they show Gisèle Pelicot alone, without the men convicted for rapes and sexual assaults while she was unconscious, knocked out with drugs that Dominique Pelicot slipped into her food and drink.
Gisèle Pelicot's statement also criticized the book itself, saying it “describes scenes of me being raped and gives an interpretation of my life that is unbearable.”
“Above all, I refuse to let my story be re-written to suggest that I was complicit with what I was subjected to,” she said, according to the statement extracts.

Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into spaceByHelen DavidsonPublished24 November 2026, 02:15 GMTUpdated 7 hours ago
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said such reports were "not new, yet they remain no less shocking", and a government spokesman said the reports were being taken "very seriously".
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the reports but dismissed stories citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutscher Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
Asked about the reports, the Nato secretary general told a press conference in Berlin alongside Merz: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."
The Western defensive alliance had a variety of response options, said Rutte.
"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary."

A comeback for the ages: Trump's influence on Huang's return to NvidiaByLaura BickerChina correspondent Published24 November 2026, 07:26 GMT
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.
Most users are pleased to see the return of the influential billionaire, who declared that he loved China, before videos appeared online of him eating noodles and drinking milk tea during a visit in May. Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets.
But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.
That's probably how Xi Jinping sees it too.
Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt".
Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Trunmp and Xi ahead of their meeting in Shenzhen last week
Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points.
For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington.

Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets.
But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.
That's probably how Xi Jinping sees it too.
Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt".
Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.

Trunmp and Xi ahead of their meeting in Shenzhen last week
Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points.
For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington.

The visuals of the historic trilateral meeting may be the only lasting impression left by the summitByAnthony ZurcherNorth America correspondentPublished19 November 2026
Donald Trump went into his trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping with little on the agenda and no clear asks – and he left with little in return.
In the end, the visuals of the meeting – the "optics", as political wags like to say – may be the only lasting impression from the summit, billed by some as a historic "Yalta 2.0" meeting of great powers.
The pomp and the ceremony, in the end, may be what the US president wanted most. Trump, bruised by his Republican Party's drubbing in midterm congressional elections earlier this month, clearly relished the global spotlight during his three-day trip to Asia and the historic nature of the first-ever US-Russia-China trilateral meeting.

That might appear to be a low bar, but it's one that could satisfy the American president.
